newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Queensland Alumina says to cut 120 workers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Queensland Alumina says to cut 120 workers.

text.p: Queensland Alumina Ltd said on Tuesday it would cut 120 jobs out of about 1,200 in the next month because of declining market conditions in the aluminium industry.
Queensland Alumina is 30.3 percent owned by Comalco Ltd.

The job cuts also reflects the refinery's unsatisfactory competitive ranking, which has forced it to immediately and significantly reduce costs by some A$10.86 million from its 1997 budget, Queensland Alumina said in a statement.
Typically, it takes two tonnes of alumina to produce one tonne of aluminium.

The decision to cut the refinery's workforce comes amid proposed expansion plans by Comalco to build its own alumina refinery at a cost of A$1 billion to take on projected increase in demand for aluminium.
An alumina refinery of its own would also provide a new outlet for Comalco's Weipa bauxite mine in northern Queensland.
Other partners in the refinery are Kaiser Aluminium Corp of the U.S. (28.3 percent), Pechiney SA of France (20 percent) and Alcan Aluminium Ltd of Canada (21.4 percent).
The refinery produces 3.3 million tonnes of alumina a year.
A spokesman for the refinery said current plans are to maintain production at full capacity in 1997.
Comalco is 67 percent owned by RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
